title: UP-9-05 Dismissal Order — Chartier v. Town of Lakeview

Katelyn S. Oldham, Attorney at Law, Law Offices of Judy Snyder, l 000 S.W. Broadway,
Suite 2400, Portland, Oregon 97205, represented Complainant.
Ken Chartier filed this complaint against the Town of Lakeview on
March l 5, 2005. Chartier alleges that he was the Fire Chief, 911 director, and
911 dispatcher for Lakeview. The 911 call center employees were members of a labor
organization. A controversy arose between the union, the Lake County commissioners,
and the Lakeview police chief. Chartier alleges that the Town first removed him from
the 911 director position and then terminated his employment as Fire Chief and
911 dispatcher, because he supported the union in the controversy, in violation of ORS
663.120.
On March 24, 2005, the Administrative Law Judge (ALJ) notified Chartier
that it appeared from the face of his complaint that the action should be dismissed for
failure to state a claim for relief under either ORS 663.120 or 243.672. The ALJ invited
Chartier to provide him with any reasoning, or disputed facts, which demonstrated that
the arguments identified by the ALJ were incorrect, or that the complaint rested on other
legal theories, so that the ALJ could determine whether it was appropriate to recommend
that the complaint be dismissed. Chartier did not file a response.
ORS 663.005 et seq. is Oregon's private sector labor relations statute.
Chartier alleges that the Town has violated ORS 663.120, which provides in part as
follows:
"* * * It is an unfair labor practice for an employer:
"( l ) To interfere with, restrain or coerce employees
in the exercise of the rights guaranteed in ORS 663.110;"
ORS 663.005 provides in part as follows:
"* * * AB used in ORS 663.005 to 663.295, unless the
context requires otherwise:
"* * * * *
"(3) 'Employee' includes any employee, and is not
limited to the employees of a particular employer unless ORS
663.005 to 663.295 explicitly states otherwise, and includes
any individual whose work has ceased as a consequence of, or
in connection with, a current labor dispute and who has not
obtained any other regular and substantially equivalent
employment, but does not include an individual:
"* * * * *
" ( e) Employed as a supervisor;
"( 4) 'Employer' includes any person acting as an agent
of an employer, directly or indirectly, but does not include:
"* * * * *
"(b) This state, or any county, city or political
subdivision or agency thereof" (Emphasis added.)
- 2 -
It is apparent on the face of the complaint that Mr. Chartier is not an
employee, and Lakeview is not an employer, within the meaning of ORS 663.005.1
We conclude that Chartier has failed to state a claim for relief. We will
dismiss the complaint.
ORDER
The complaint is dismissed.
DATED this l!-1-"' day of May 2005.
Paul B. Gamson, Chair
Rita E. Thomas, Board Member
*
James W. Kasameyer, Board Member
*Member Kasameyer absent on the date of signing.
This Order may be appealed pursuant to ORS 183.482.
1 Lakeview is a public employer under the Public Employees Collective Bargaining Act
(PECBA). ORS 243.650(20). However, the allegations of the complaint, which we assume to be
true for purposes of this Order, establish that Chartier was not a "public employee" as defined
in the PECBA, and therefore has no rights under that statute. ORS 243.650(19) and Flanders v.
Bay Area Hospital, Case No. UP-136-92, 14 PECBR240, 244 (1992). TheALJ notified Chartier
of this information and asked Chartier to provide any disputed facts or reasoning that shows it
is incorrect. Chartier did not respond.
